references.text: The Pharisees and the scribes grumbled and said, 'This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.' The same type of criticism from the Pharisees about Jesus associating with sinners.

When Jesus forgave sins, the Pharisees and the scribes thought to themselves that this was blasphemy. Here too, religious leaders react negatively in their thoughts to Jesus' relationship with sin and sinners.
All who saw it grumbled and said, 'He has gone to stay with a sinful man.' Again, Jesus is criticized for having fellowship with sinners, here Zacchaeus.
The Pharisees asked the disciples, 'Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?' The Pharisees' criticism of Jesus' association with sinners is a recurring theme.
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, 'Look, a glutton and a wine drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!' Jesus was accused of being a friend of sinners.
The Samaritan woman said to Jesus, 'Sir, I see that you are a prophet.' The question of whether Jesus is a prophet who knows people's inner lives – in contrast to the Pharisees' doubt.
The Pharisees called Jesus a sinner and refused to acknowledge him. Here the Pharisee rejects Jesus' prophetic identity, just as the Pharisees in John refuse to acknowledge him.
The people glorified God and said, 'A great prophet has arisen among us.' Shortly before this event, Jesus was recognized by the people as a prophet, but the Pharisee doubts this.
Those who say, 'Keep away, do not come near me, for I am holy to you.' The Pharisees' attitude of keeping away from sinners is mirrored in this Isaiah word about self-righteousness.

The Pharisees and their scribes grumbled and said to the disciples, 'Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?' The same pattern of Pharisaic criticism against Jesus for associating with sinners.

Those who were at the table began to say to themselves, 'Who is this who even forgives sins?' Here too, the guests question Jesus' identity and authority, as an extension of the Pharisees' doubt in verse 39.
